From: Maya Patel <maya@quantshore.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 14:32:00 -0800
Subject: QuantShore LLM platform evaluation — perf targets & timeline

Aditya,

Thanks for the intro last week. QuantShore has kicked off a short bakeoff to decide on the inference platform for our next-gen quant models. We have a competitive offer on the table (HelixAI) and need to validate two things for any supplier:

- Sustained throughput: 20 inference req/s at 512-token context for a 6k-param LLM family
- Tail latency: 95th < 220ms for production mix
- Deterministic scaling to 3x baseline within 72 hours

We'd like Redwood to run a short proof-of-concept benchmark against those metrics and share an apples-to-apples cost comparison (per-1000-token). I'm attaching the RFP/requirements (quantshore_rfp.pdf).

Can you (1) confirm you can run the benchmark in our preferred region (us-west-2), (2) give a rough timeline, and (3) share any constraints on comparing your hosted vs dedicated offerings? We also need to understand contract term flexibility — our procurement is pushing for a 24-month committed discount with an option to expand capacity.

Best,
Maya
Director, ML Platforms
QuantShore

Subject: Re: QuantShore LLM platform evaluation — perf targets & timeline

Maya — appreciate the clear requirements and the RFP. Short answers up front: yes, we can run a focussed benchmark in us-west-2 and deliver a detailed apples-to-apples report; timeline ~7 business days for baseline bench and cost model; yes we support hosted, Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) and our Private/VPC options — we’ll include equivalent config comparisons.

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick kickoff call tomorrow to align on exact model family and dataset slices (30m).
2) We run a controlled benchmark (7 business days) with agreed load profile + 95th latency percentiles.
3) Deliver bench report + cost per-1k-tokens comparison + upgrade/scale proposal.

I’ve attached our suggested PoC scope (redwood_poc_scope.pdf) — it maps your targets to the workload we’ll run. Vivek (cc) will own the bench execution; Marissa will scope commercial options for retention/commit terms.

Few notes for procurement: if you share the HelixAI terms (pricing & committed months), that helps us model a competitive renewal/expansion package.

Talk soon—
Aditya Rao

Aditya / Maya,

Quick procurement note — HelixAI has already tabled a term sheet: 24 months, 25% off list for committed baseline (6 GPUs equivalent), plus a further 10% rebate if we hit certain usage bands in Q2. They’ve also offered a 30-day performance validation period.

Helix’s pricing is aggressive; if Redwood wants to be competitive we need a firm commercial signal (discount + capacity uplift path) — otherwise the execs will likely default to the incumbent offer.

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Eugene Ward <eward@quantshore.com>, aditya_rao@redwood.com, maya@quantshore.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Nov 2027 10:15:00 -0800

Eugene / Maya — thanks for the visibility. A few technical clarifications and an initial play we can run quickly:

- Model family: if you can confirm the exact model weights (or a representative open checkpoint) we’ll ensure kernel parity and matching tokenization.
- For 20 req/s sustained at 512 tokens, our Dedicated pool with mixed-precision quantization and smart KV caching typically hits your 95th target on comparable models; we’ll run both hosted optimized path and a Dedicated-config to show delta.
- Bursting to 3x baseline in 72 hours is achievable via reserved pool autoscale + burst capacity; we’ll outline the costs for warm vs cold capacity.

Commercially — we can do a retention/scale proposal:
- 12-month committed baseline (option to convert to 24 months after trial)
- 20% off list for year 1 on committed baseline
- One-time $50k trial credit to cover bench infra + early migration effort
- SLA: 99.9% uptime for dedicated pools; priority support during bench

I’m attaching a short bench plan that Vivek will execute with your team (qsh_bench_plan.md). This gives us a clear way to compare Helix’s 24-month offer.

If QuantShore can share the Helix term sheet (even as a redacted image) we’ll return a firm competitive counter within 48 hours after the baseline bench.

—Vivek
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: QuantShore LLM platform evaluation — perf targets & timeline (Escalation: competitive price pressure)

Marissa / Neha — looping you in. QuantShore is in an active bakeoff and procurement just shared HelixAI’s commercial terms (24m, 25% + usage rebate). We have a technical path to meet the perf targets and a bench timeline, but to close this deal we should consider a stronger retention package.

Recommendation for an approved counter (to present after baseline bench completes):
- 24-month committed contract at 22% off year-1 list (split-year pricing: 20% year 1 base + 2% additional if they commit to Q2 expansion targets)
- $75k one-time migration/benchmark credit (covers full bench and proof workload for month 1)
- 2-month performance validation window with option to exit if SLA not met (gives procurement parity with Helix’s 30-day)
- Executive sponsor intro and quarterly business reviews for 12 months

Asks: can we get Marissa approval to use $75k credit vs the $50k Vivek proposed? Also need Neha’s sign-off on the 22% list discount and the 24-month commitment structure. If you prefer, I can convert this into a clean term sheet and present to their procurement.

Quick context: QuantShore is a high-visibility logo in the quant vertical. If we lose this they’ll likely consolidate with the competitor for at least one year — high risk to pipeline.

Thanks,
Aditya
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
